From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 21 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: High p99 tail and QPS drop for gen-api in us-west-2

Team —

Alerts just tripped across the gen-api fleet in us-west-2. Summary: p99 latency jumped from ~280ms to ~1.6s over the past 10m while overall QPS to gen-api dropped ~40% (some clients stayed steady, others experienced throttles). Dashboard and initial SRE traces attached.

Quick facts:
- Alert: INC-20270521-37 (link below)
- Top symptoms: p99 spike, rising retry rates from downstream proxies, sudden drop in concurrent tokens served on several nodes
- Affected model pool: genapi-main-v2 (float32 and int8 variants)
- Region: us-west-2 (primary customer impact: BrightCart)

Immediate asks:
1) Karthik — can infra confirm whether kernel scheduling or GPU contention shows up in the traces? I see some long GPU busy periods but need confirmation.
2) Marissa/Product — do we want to flip routing to the compact model (genapi-compact-v1) as a temporary fallback? What are the known quality regressions to call out?
3) Vivek — need customer comms once we scope impact. Drafting a short note for ops@brightcart.com would help.

Attaching svc_trace_20270521.zip and a quick dashboard screenshot. Logging also points to a batch window increase around 08:58.

Soojin
Soojin Lee
SRE — Redwood Inference

Heads-up on product tradeoffs and suggested customer messaging.

Tradeoffs for fallback to genapi-compact-v1:
- Latency: compact model consistently lower tail latency at similar QPS (good)
- Quality: hallucination rate increases on long-context prompts; token-level perplexity rises ~7% on our internal eval set for checkout flows
- Cost: compact model saves ~22% per-token CPU/GPU time — may be worth flagging as actionable cost savings if customer accepts quality tradeoff

Suggested customer bullet points to include if we switch:
- We are rolling traffic to a lower-latency model to preserve availability while we investigate a production scheduling issue.
- Expected change: slight drop in some long-form generation fidelity; core checkout flows are unaffected in >95% of test cases.
- Timeline: temporary; we will revert to genapi-main-v2 after the root cause is fixed and validated (ETA TBD).

Also: Product asks for engineering if you can confirm: can the fallback be applied per-tenant (BrightCart) without global impact? If yes, we'll request it.

Marissa

Subject: Re: Fwd: High p99 tail and QPS drop for gen-api in us-west-2

Triage update (short version):
- Root cause signal: scheduler kernel and batch coalescing combination causing increased per-batch GPU stall under a narrow sequence-length distribution. Specifically, a kernel upgrade rolled two weeks ago changed a heuristic for continuous batching; under certain request arrival patterns this causes larger-than-expected batch accumulation and longer kernel warmups.
- Evidence: GPU busy intervals in svc_trace_20270521.zip show contiguous busy windows matching the latency spikes; host metrics show no memory pressure or thermal events.

Immediate mitigation (low-risk):
1) Reduce max batch window from 12ms -> 4ms for genapi-main-v2 in us-west-2 (config change). This will reduce batching efficiency slightly but drop p99 significantly. ETA: 15m to push and validate on canaries.
2) If canary validates, apply per-tenant routing change for BrightCart to genapi-compact-v1 (fallback) for up to 2h while we push a kernel heuristic tweak. Per-tenant routing is supported; need CS ops to run the routing change (I can provide exact command).

Longer fix: revert kernel heuristic change or add an adaptive threshold based on sequence length distribution — timeline 1-2 days for dev + canary + rollout.

Commands (internal runbook snippet):
- To reduce batch window (canary): infractl set cluster genapi-main-v2 --region us-west-2 --batch-window-ms 4 --target canary
- Per-tenant fallback (CS-assisted): csctl route set --tenant brightcart --model genapi-compact-v1 --duration 2h --note "temporary fallback during scheduling investigation"

I will queue the config change to canaries now if you approve.

Karthik
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

Subject: [Customer Note] Temporary availability mitigation for gen-api in us-west-2

Eva / BrightCart Ops —

Quick note from Redwood: we detected an infrastructure scheduling issue in our us-west-2 gen-api fleet that caused elevated tail latency and intermittent throughput drops affecting a subset of customers this morning. We are taking a conservative approach to preserve availability for your production traffic.

What we did:
- Reduced internal batch-window heuristics for gen-api canaries and validated improved latency.
- Temporarily routed BrightCart traffic to a lower-latency model (genapi-compact-v1) for the next 2 hours while we complete deeper validation.

What to expect:
- Latency should return to normal (p99 reduced to target range).
- You may notice modest differences in long-form generation quality on rare prompts — this is expected and temporary.

Next steps:
- Our engineering team is pushing a kernel scheduling tweak; we expect to re-evaluate and, if validated, restore genapi-main-v2 within 24–48 hours.
- We will notify you before reverting traffic.

If you prefer not to accept the temporary fallback, we can instead throttle burst traffic or attempt a regional reroute; please advise and we will act immediately.

Apologies for the interruption — we know reliability is critical and we are prioritizing a full fix.

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Product Operations — Redwood Inference
